title: Brightening serum for post-acne hyperpigmentation in Fitzpatrick IV to VI: a planned open-label study at an academic centre, brand collaborator
headline: A 20-person, open-label, single-centre study of a French cosmetic brightening serum for post-acne dark marks in medium to deep skin is registered to start in Sept 2026; no results, no control arm, and the brand is a collaborator.
evidenceTier: Trial registry record, read in full; no results
fit: Pigment-prone skin: Partial. Right population (Fitzpatrick IV to VI), weak design.
displaces: Would replace an existing brightening serum step, not add one.
regions: Global (cosmetic; the registry record names the brand Caudalie as collaborator)
estimateNote: Prices marked EST are my guesses, not looked up.
buzzCheck: Prices not looked up; cannot judge whether price tracks evidence.
summaryPoints: Observation (registry record read): Weill Cornell Medicine, New York; n=20 planned; adults with Fitzpatrick IV to VI, moderate to severe post-acne PIH (PAHPI score 8 or more), mild acne only; 12 weeks; primary outcome is change in PAHPI at week 12; secondary outcomes are tolerability and a patient-reported stigma questionnaire.
Observation: status not yet recruiting; start Sept 2026; primary completion 15 Jan 2027. Participants must use no other facial products during the study.

Observation: the product is described only as a brightening serum ('Vinoperfect brightening serum'). I did not open a brand or retailer page this run, so ingredients, concentrations and price are not verified.
Limits: no comparator; the brand is a collaborator; 20 people.
toneData: Fitzpatrick IV to VI by protocol, any ethnicity
fitLine: Population is relevant; a small open-label brand-linked study will tell me little about whether the serum beats a plain moisturizer plus sunscreen.

fitAxes.why: The protocol asks participants to avoid sun and use sun protection as part of the routine.
